transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-13
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Partnerships), Liam O'Connell (ArgonGrid VP Partnerships), Maya Patel (ArgonGrid Head Cloud Integrations), Ethan Zhao (ArgonGrid Lead Infra Eng), Nora Kim (ArgonGrid Solutions Arch)

Summary (auto): Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and ArgonGrid. Discussed go-to-market fit, integration patterns (marketplace vs private deployments), high-level technical constraints (VPC peering, private control plane, KMS), and benchmarking asks. Agreed next steps: share partner one-pager, perf spreadsheet, schedule technical deep-dive for network and security.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, AE on the partnership program at Redwood. With me is Daniel our SE, and Priya from partnerships. How are you all?
[00:10] Liam O'Connell: Good, thanks. Liam here. Excited to learn more about Redwood, we've been looking at inference partners.
[00:16] Maya Patel: Hey all, Maya. Quick note - we're mostly focused on cloud-integrated managed infra for enterprise customers, lots of regulated workloads.
[00:22] Daniel Cho: Great. Quick housekeeping - we'll do a short intro from both sides, then cover where you see fit for a partnership, tech constraints, and then action items. Sound good?
[00:30] Nora Kim: Yep.
[00:32] Ethan Zhao: Sounds good.
[00:34] Sofia Martinez: I'll kick off - Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform. We run hosted, dedicated pools, and private deployments. We focus on predictable latency, cost controls, and observability for customers. We work a lot with partners who provide cloud/GPU capacity or systems integrators.
[00:46] Mason (transcription glitch - speaker mislabelled): sorry, small tangential - Redwood's dedicated stuff, we call it Redwoo Dedicatede a lot in docs, but it's just Dedicated. Anyway.
[00:54] Liam O'Connell: Cool. High level from ArgonGrid - we operate a distributed GPU-based cloud with regions in NA and EU, aim to partner for managed CI/CD style deployments for enterprise. We do private link / VPC peering and have pipeline tooling for customers to bring their own model or use marketplace images.
[01:09] Priya Rao: Nice. Is ArgonGrid looking to be a sales channel, hosting partner, or both?
[01:14] Liam O'Connell: Both ideally. Channel for mutual customers but also to run Redwood Private stacks for customers who want ArgonGrid-managed infra.
[01:20] Daniel Cho: Understood. On the tech side, do you have standard H100 / A100 offerings? Any custom SKUs or single-tenant racks?
[01:28] Maya Patel: We have A100s and H100s; we've started offering dedicated racks for some enterprise customers (single-tenant) - it's more common for regulated workloads. We also offer volume discounts.
[01:38] Daniel Cho: Good. A couple of things we often see: network egress latency for model weights, KMS integrations for key management, and audit logs for SOC2 customers. Do you already provide KMS/HSM integrations or do customers bring their own?
[01:51] Ethan Zhao: We integrate with AWS KMS and a few third-party HSMs. We can offer Bring-Your-Own-KMS or manage keys via our service. For SOC2 we've got an audit pipeline and can surface logs, but we typically need to map fields for each partner.
[02:04] Sofia Martinez: Perfect — that aligns with common enterprise asks. For Redwood Private, we support a private control plane and customer-managed networking/policies. We also have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments.
[02:16] Nora Kim: How does the control plane work? Are you running anything in our VPC or is it fully customer-hosted?
[02:22] Daniel Cho: We have options. For many partners we offer a private control plane that can be run inside the partner's cloud account (customer-managed). There's also an option for just the data plane on-prem with Redwood managing orchestration remotely—depends on the risk model.
[02:35] Liam O'Connell: On the commercial side, do you have a partner revenue share or marketplace listing?
[02:40] Priya Rao: We do partner programs - we can discuss revenue share or referral programs. For marketplace listings, we have patterns: either hosted API integration or a marketplace image for Baremetal/VM-based deployments.
[02:51] Maya Patel: For regulated customers we need clear SLAs and support windows. Do you support SLA tiers for Dedicated/Private customers?
[02:58] Sofia Martinez: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, plus priority support as an add-on.
[03:05] Daniel Cho: If it's helpful, we can walk through a sample topology.
[03:08] Ethan Zhao: That would be great. Our typical customer topology: front-door load balancer, VPC peering to partner infra, internal model serving subnet, and a private S3 for model artifacts. We also use Vault for secrets.
[03:21] Daniel Cho: OK, so a typical Redwood integration would sit in the serving subnet, with the model artifacts in your S3 and KMS for encryption. We attach KV cache and batching controllers inside the RD runtime. One thing to note: continuous batching and KV cache state can be pinned to GPU nodes for faster response, so network hops matter.
[03:38] Maya Patel: How do you handle multi-tenant on the same racks? Noise neighbors are a concern for some of our customers.
[03:44] Daniel Cho: We offer dedicated pools for single-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors; for multi-tenant we have resource isolation and QoS settings, but performance variability can still exist. For strict SLAs we recommend dedicated racks.
[03:56] Liam O'Connell: About model size — most of our customers do 7B-33B models for chat, some 70B for fine-tuning. What does Redwood recommend for throughput/latency tradeoffs?
[04:06] Daniel Cho: For 2k token chat workloads, quantized 8-bit models on H100 give good cost/latency tradeoffs, but for deterministic outputs and complex tool-calling sometimes higher precision is needed. Redwood Optimize can provide quantization and batching suggestions by workload.
[04:22] Nora Kim: Any client-side integration work? Do you expose an SDK?
[04:26] Sofia Martinez: Yes, we have REST/SDK interfaces for generation, embeddings, and tool calling. For partners we share SDK integration guides and sample Lambda/Cloud Run deployments.
[04:36] Liam O'Connell: On security: customers want SSO, RBAC, and full audit trails. How granular is RBAC?
[04:42] Daniel Cho: We support role-based access controls with SSO (SAML/OIDC), and granular per-route permissions plus audit logs that can be exported to your SIEM.
[04:52] Maya Patel: A couple of customers also need data residency in EU. Do you have model hosting region controls?
[04:58] Sofia Martinez: Yes, customers can pin model versions to regions. We also support routing policies to keep data within region and automated fallback to region-compatible variants.
[05:09] Liam O'Connell: Great. Let's talk about a pilot — what would you need from us to run a small POC?
[05:15] Daniel Cho: For a POC we usually want: a topology diagram, expected token volume and latency SLOs, sample prompts or workloads, and access to a staging environment. If it's Dedicated on ArgonGrid, we'd need capacity details (GPU type, NICs, rack isolation).
[05:29] Ethan Zhao: We can provide a diagram and traffic profile. Our initial pilot idea is 2 racks of H100 for 3 weeks, target 2000 concurrent requests/day with 95th p99 latency under 600ms. Is that a reasonable ask?
[05:42] Daniel Cho: 600ms p95 for 2k tokens on H100 is in the realm of achievable but depends on batching and KV cache warm state. We'll run a perf calc and share.
[05:51] Priya Rao: Commercially, we can offer a pilot credit and help with onboarding.
[05:55] Liam O'Connell: Excellent. Any regulatory blockers? E.g., we sometimes need customers to run in air-gapped mode.
[06:01] Sofia Martinez: We have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. It requires a slightly longer onboarding and validation window but it's supported.
[06:10] Maya Patel: On telemetry — we need to surface token-level cost and route breakdown for billing. Do you expose that?
[06:16] Daniel Cho: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We can hook your billing pipeline to those metrics.
[06:26] Liam O'Connell: Are there any known gotchas with HSM or KMS rotation?
[06:31] Daniel Cho: Key rotation is supported; we recommend coordinating rotation windows. For some managed HSMs there's a brief rekey window that can affect decryption latency; we can document recommended rotation schedules.
[06:42] Nora Kim: For the marketplace flow: do you provide images that run on top of our infra or do you prefer using your control plane image?
[06:48] Sofia Martinez: Both models are used. For marketplace we'd provide an image and Helm chart for self-hosted installs. For managed listings we can run the control plane with permissions in the partner account.
[06:59] Ethan Zhao: For networking, we need to know what ports are required and egress patterns.
[07:04] Daniel Cho: We'll share a network integration doc; generally we need TLS outbound to telemetry endpoints (if using managed control plane), internal gRPC for data plane, and S3 connectivity for artifacts. We can provide an allowlist.
[07:18] Liam O'Connell: Pricing - is there list pricing for Dedicated racks or is it custom?
[07:23] Sofia Martinez: For Dedicated it's usually a reserved capacity contract with monthly commits, we have standard templates but most enterprise deals are customized. For marketplace images there's a per-instance or per-token billing option.
[07:35] Maya Patel: A couple of our customers care about model provenance and lineage - can Redwood attach model metadata and handle signed artifacts?
[07:42] Daniel Cho: Yes, we support signed model artifacts and metadata tracking. We can integrate with your artifact registry or S3 with signed manifests.
[07:52] Nora Kim: Any partners live today with a similar integration we could talk to?
[07:56] Priya Rao: We have a few channel partners and cloud partners — we can share references after the call.
[08:02] Sofia Martinez: Ok, let's summarize next steps. We'll share the partner one-pager and the integration checklist, Daniel will run the perf calc for the H100 racks, and ArgonGrid will share topology and traffic profile. We'll schedule a technical deep dive focused on SOC2, KMS, and VPC peering for the week of 12/20.
[08:20] Liam O'Connell: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:23] Maya Patel: If you can include a sample SLA template and a rough pricing band for a 2-rack pilot that would be helpful.
[08:30] Sofia Martinez: We'll include that in the follow-up. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email with attachments.
[08:37] Ethan Zhao: Thanks.
[08:38] Nora Kim: Thanks, bye.

Notes: small transcription artifacts present (speaker names occasionally off). References shared: integration checklist (link placeholder), benchmark spreadsheet (link placeholder), partner one-pager (link placeholder).
